justifications.functional_suitability: WebRTC Media Server Containers (SFUs), AI Symptom Checker Container, Granular Consent Manager and Clinician Dashboard & Handoff Container cover R-01, R-03, R-04. E-prescriptions rely on a generic Notification Gateway with no clear prescription service. Patients have no web or app container.
justifications.performance_efficiency: SFU Core Engine provides simulcast and dynamic bitrate scaling; Async Queue & Retry Manager (Pub/Sub) decouples dispatch; Telemetry Exporter gives metrics. Gaps: no caching, autoscaling or capacity targets are shown, and Redis Session Manager is the only data-access optimization.
justifications.compatibility: HL7 FHIR appears only on the Pharmacies relationship, and national EU e-prescription standards are mentioned only as 'national e-prescriptions'. No adapter or integration component exists per country or standard; the Notification Gateway is generic.
justifications.usability: Clinicians have a Clinician Dashboard; Patients and Compliance Officers have no dedicated interface container. The Istio/Envoy ingress is said to be optimized for rural connections. Consent UI and compliance reporting channels are not modelled.
justifications.reliability: SFU simulcast supports degraded mode below 300 kbit/s; Async Queue & Retry Manager provides retries and DLQs; regional GKE clusters isolate failures. Gaps: no multi-zone, failover, backup or recovery mechanisms, and no offline fallback for consultations.
justifications.security: Istio mTLS and authorization policies, DTLS-SRTP and JWT, Cloud KMS CMEK, Crypto-Shredding Manager, VPC Service Controls, Secret Manager, and Audit Logger with Fluent Bit PII stripping cover R-05 and R-07. Gaps: identity provider/clinician authentication, model-version logging, and cross-region consent flow are unspecified.
justifications.maintainability: Decomposition into separate containers and components is reasonable, with a Localization & Regulatory Service and Audit Traceability Worker. Weaknesses: the model is inconsistent—Regional GKE Clusters treated as a container holding services, a self-referencing Audit Traceability Worker, and actors appearing as components.
justifications.portability: Kubernetes, Istio, containers and open SFUs (Jitsi/Mediasoup) are portable, but the design relies on GCP-specific services (Cloud KMS, Pub/Sub, Cloud Run, VPC Service Controls, Cloud Logging) with no abstraction layer, and covers only the two named GCP regions.

sensitivity_points: No autoscaling or SFU capacity sizing stated
Join time depends on signalling, which is not modelled
tradeoffs: mTLS mesh overhead versus join latency
PERF-01.justification: SFUs on regional GKE can scale in principle, but there is no autoscaling, capacity plan, signalling service or session routing. 5,000 concurrent sessions and a 10 s join time are not addressed.

sensitivity_points: Synchronous audit logging on the request path
Inference scaling and model serving are unspecified
tradeoffs: Full audit logging versus 3 s latency
PERF-02.justification: A stateless triage controller with Redis sessions behind the mesh is plausible. No autoscaling, model-serving or GPU details are given, and the audit write may sit on the critical path. 50k/hour at p95 under 3 s is unproven.

sensitivity_points: Simulcast and bitrate scaling cover only the video stream
Clinical notes persistence on connection drop is unspecified
tradeoffs: Video quality versus continuity at low bandwidth
AVAIL-01.justification: The SFU provides simulcast and dynamic bitrate scaling for connections below 300 kbit/s, which is a strong mechanism for degraded video. There is no audio-only fallback, no client-side note buffering and no reconnect mechanism, so the no-loss-of-notes measure is unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: No multi-zone or in-region DR design
Failover must stay inside the US
tradeoffs: Strict residency versus cross-region failover options
AVAIL-02.justification: Regional clusters keep data in the US region, but there is no failover, multi-zone or backup/restore design, no RTO mechanism and no within-US recovery path. Restoring service within 1 hour is not supported.

sensitivity_points: Dispatch logic is not separated per national standard
Clinician dashboard also dispatches directly to pharmacies
tradeoffs: A single gateway is simple but couples all standards
MOD-01.justification: No standards-specific adapter or anti-corruption layer exists. The dispatch controller is monolithic, and the dashboard shows a direct pharmacy path, so changes for a new country would not be confined to one adapter. FHIR is only mentioned at the context level.

sensitivity_points: Model version is not explicitly captured in the logs
No model registry or versioned deployment
tradeoffs: PII stripping in logs versus traceability of inputs
MOD-02.justification: The Audit Logger records inputs and the container is deployable on Kubernetes, but there is no model registry, versioning, canary or rollback mechanism, and no explicit model-version link. PII stripping may remove traceability data.

sensitivity_points: Consent check is not enforced at the data store
tradeoffs: Strict isolation versus legitimate cross-border care access
SEC-01.justification: The consent manager, residency enforcer and clinician-to-regulatory consent check are the right concepts. There is no explicit cross-region access path, deny-by-default policy or access-request logging, and the logging path strips PII, so enforcement and auditability are unproven.

sensitivity_points: No propagation mechanism to downstream recipients
Crypto-shredding is per patient, not per purpose
tradeoffs: Crypto-shredding is irreversible versus purpose-level revocation
SEC-02.justification: A consent manager and audit worker exist, but there is no consent-change event propagation, no research data sharing component, and no verification mechanism. Per-patient crypto-shredding is too coarse for withdrawing a single purpose.
